news.author: Rishabh Mishra
news.content:
U.S. stock futures are pointing to a broadly lower open early Wednesday as Wall Street digests early midterm election results showing key Democratic Senate victories and a shifting geopolitical landscape.

The Polymarket traders, a Polygon (CRYPTO: POL) based prediction platform, have turned heavily bearish for the Nov. 4 trading session. The “S&P 500 (SPX) Up or Down on November 4?” contract currently reflects a 22% chance of a higher open.

Why That Number Matters

Traders are balancing negative equity futures against fluctuating energy markets and a packed economic docket:

  • Negative Index Futures: A tech-led pullback is dragging major benchmarks into the red. Nasdaq 100 futures dropped 1.11%. S&P 500 futures fell 0.75%, Dow Jones futures slipped 0.55%, and Russell 2000 futures declined 0.47%.
  • Geopolitics & Oil: President Donald Trump signaled that the U.S. may not need another immediate military strike against Iran, stating, “We seem to be getting everything we want,” though he emphasized the military remains “locked and loaded.” Meanwhile, Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.) vowed that Democrats will stop funding the Iran offensive, citing the need to lower domestic energy and food costs. Energy markets ticked slightly higher on the mixed signals; Brent crude rose 0.69% to $104.32 a barrel, while WTI crude climbed 0.48% to $96.55 a barrel.
  • Earnings & Eco Data: Wednesday’s economic slate features October’s ADP national employment report and September’s U.S. trade balance at 8:30 a.m. ET, followed by U.S. services PMI and ISM services PMI data starting at 9:45 a.m. ET. The corporate calendar is headlined by Arm Holdings PLC (NASDAQ:ARM), McDonald’s Corp. (NYSE:MCD), Novo Nordisk A/S (NYSE:NVO), Qualcomm Inc. (NASDAQ:QCOM), and Uber Technologies Inc. (NYSE:UBER).

The Bull Case and Market Outlook

Fundstrat’s Tom Lee believes the recent tech stock pullback has concluded, stating, “I think we are at the bottom.” Lee maintains his target for the S&P 500 to finish the year above 8,200, emphasizing that the underlying market for AI remains very tight and demand is resilient.

Lee identified the midterm elections as a crucial “clearing event” for the market. While prediction markets and polls heavily favored a Democratic sweep, early results confirming Democratic Senate victories in Georgia, North Carolina, and Virginia align with those expectations. Lee noted that resolving this political uncertainty often helps sidelined cash re-enter the market, allowing equities to climb the proverbial “wall of worry” into a strong year-end finish.

How the Previous Bet Played Out

The Nov. 3 Polymarket contract resolved “Up.” The contract recorded $47,910 in total trading volume.

On Tuesday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY) and Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (NASDAQ:QQQ), which track the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100, respectively, closed mixed. SPY rose 0.30% to $754.35, while QQQ advanced 0.62% to $685.28. Meanwhile, the Dow tracker, State Street SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (NYSE:DIA), ended 0.44% lower at $517.06.

news.author: Avi Kapoor
news.content:
The CNN Money Fear and Greed Index showed no change in overall market sentiment, while the index remained in the “Extreme Fear” zone on Tuesday.

U.S. stocks settled mixed on Tuesday, with the Nasdaq Composite gaining more than 200 points during the session amid a rebound in chip stocks.

Shares of Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) fell around 2% on Tuesday after the company announced that its gross margin would land between 45% and 46% in the December quarter. That’s below the 46.3% analysts expected, mainly because of higher memory costs.

Pfizer Inc. (NYSE:PFE) on Tuesday reported upbeat results for the third quarter. Shares of Aehr Test Systems (NASDAQ:AEHR) jumped over 26% after the company reported better-than-expected first-quarter financial results and raised its FY27 sales guidance above estimates.

Treasury yields climbed after the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported 7.5 million job openings for September, topping expectations of 7.1 million ahead of the midterm elections. Factory orders increased 1.8% in September, beating the 1.2% forecast after a 0.3% gain in August.

Most sectors on the S&P 500 closed on a negative note, with consumer staples, materials and energy stocks recording the biggest losses on Tuesday. However, industrials and information technology stocks were among the top performers.

The Dow Jones closed lower by around 197 points to 51,786.72 on Tuesday. The S&P 500 rose 0.36% to 7,568.92, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 0.83% at 25,372.01 during Tuesday’s session.

Investors are awaiting earnings results from McDonald’s Corp (NYSE:MCD), Uber Technologies Inc (NYSE:UBER) and Qualcomm Inc (NASDAQ:QCOM) today.

What is CNN Business Fear & Greed Index?

At a current reading of 19, the index remained in the “Extreme Fear” zone on Tuesday, versus a prior reading of 19.

The Fear & Greed Index is a measure of the current market sentiment. It is based on the premise that higher fear exerts pressure on stock prices, while higher greed has the opposite effect. The index is calculated based on seven equal-weighted indicators. The index ranges from 0 to 100, where 0 represents maximum fear and 100 signals maximum greed.

Photo via Shutterstock
news.headline: Nasdaq Jumps Over 200 Points as Chip Stocks Gain: Fear & Greed Index Remains in ‘Extreme Fear’ Zone
news.summary: Markets closed mixed as CNN Fear & Greed stayed at 19 (Extreme Fear); Nasdaq rose 0.83%, Dow fell, Apple dropped and Aehr surged 26%.

news.author: Rishabh Mishra
news.content:
Historical market data shows a divided congressional government produces the highest average returns for the S&P 500. At the same time, a Republican president paired with a Democratic Congress results in the lowest historical market gains.

The ‘Worst Possible Combination’

When factoring in the political affiliation of the sitting president, the dynamic shifts significantly. According to Ryan Detrick‘s historical data, “The worst possible combination is a Republican President and a Democratic Congress.”

This specific political makeup—a scenario that would apply to Donald Trump assuming the presidency alongside a Democratic-majority Congress—historically yields an average annual S&P 500 return of just 4.9%.

Detrick observed that markets were actively pricing in this data, adding, “Futures seem to agree so far.” Responding to a question about whether this 4.9% figure was primarily driven by the Global Financial Crisis, Detrick stated, “It is the most likely scenario at 22 times. So it is somewhat, but some other bad years in there for sure.”

Read Also: Tom Lee Says 'We Are at the Bottom' as Tech Sell-Off Rocks Markets — But He Still Sees S&P 500 Above 8,200 By Year-End

The ‘Best Scenario’ for Stocks

A split Congress yields an average S&P 500 annual return of 15.1%, based on historical data spanning 1951 to 2025. Sharing the data on X, Detrick, stated, “Good reminder that the best scenario for stocks is a split Congress.”

When looking strictly at congressional makeup without factoring in the executive branch, Detrick noted that “A Democrat controlled Congress is the worst scenario historically,” as that setup averages a 6.7% return compared to 11.3% for a Republican-controlled Congress.

Historical Market Context

The data, sourced from Carson Investment Research and FactSet, tracks market performance starting with the 82nd Congress. Under a Republican president with a Republican Congress, the index averages a 7.6% return, while a Republican president with a split Congress averages 13.7%.

Conversely, a Democratic president paired with a split Congress yields the highest specific combination return at 17.0%, while a Democratic president with a Republican Congress averages 16.3%. A Democratic president paired with a Democratic Congress averages an 8.6% return.

How Has the Stock Market Performed?

The S&P 500 index has advanced 10.36% year-to-date. Similarly, the Nasdaq Composite index was up 9.19%, and the Dow Jones gained 7.04% YTD.

On Tuesday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY) and Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (NASDAQ:QQQ), which track the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100, respectively, closed mixed. SPY rose 0.30% to $754.35, while QQQ advanced 0.62% to $685.28. Meanwhile, the Dow tracker, State Street SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (NYSE:DIA), ended 0.44% lower at $517.06.

Read Also: Apple’s Siri AI Could Become a Paid Upgrade — CEO John Ternus Reveals Plans to Charge for More Server-Side Apple Intelligence Usage

news.author: Namrata Sen
news.content:
CNBC’s Jim Cramer said that technology leadership may be broadening beyond the Magnificent Seven stocks, as semiconductor and networking stocks regained momentum.

On Tuesday, Cramer said on "Mad Money” that Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA), Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT), Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL) and Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) have struggled to sustain their recent rallies.

Tuesday’s advances in Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO) and Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) helped support major indexes. Cramer said the moves could indicate investors are rotating toward different technology winners.

He highlighted Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) and Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) after both companies delivered strong quarterly results following Tuesday’s closing bell. Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) also drew attention after its shares closed nearly 6% higher.

"Tech’s trying to make a stand here. It’s just not the tech that’s led us for the last few years," Cramer said. He added, "I want to believe that non-magnificent tech can lead us,” but cautioned investors against getting overly optimistic based on a single positive trading session.

Cramer also cited resistance to data-center construction, including community concerns about electricity costs and water consumption. Smaller developers, including IREN (NASDAQ:IREN), Nebius Group (NASDAQ:NBIS) and CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV), could face greater exposure to those challenges, said the CNBC host, while larger companies such as Amazon.com (NASDAQ:AMZN) have more resources to find alternative locations.

Cramer said he "would like to wait for the crescendo” before committing too much money back into tech.

Read Also: Exclusive: Investors Are Watching AI Revenue Growth Against CapEx as Companies Face Pressure to Prove Returns, Wall Street Veteran Says: ‘The Bar Rises With the Size of the Spend'

Tech Selloff Deepens Investor Concerns

Cramer’s caution follows a sharp deterioration in sentiment around big tech stocks. Intel Corp. (NASDAQ:INTC) shares have plunged 47.89% over a month after the company issued a disappointing fourth-quarter outlook at the end of October.

Semiconductor stocks lost around $1 trillion in market value last Friday. The CNBC commentator warned that market volatility could persist as investors question whether massive AI spending can justify elevated technology valuations. He advised investors against trying to time a tech-sector bottom and instead focusing on quality stocks caught in broad sell-offs.

At the same time, Tech analyst Dan Ives called the tech selloff a "gut check" for companies facing pressure to prove they can monetize AI investments. While describing the downturn as a "disaster for tech investors," he urged investors not to panic and identified Palantir Technologies Inc. (NASDAQ: PLTR), Microsoft, Nvidia and Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL) as stocks to hold over the next five years.

news.content: Chinese AI developers have placed orders for approximately 6 million NVIDIA RTX Pro 5500 chips, valued at roughly $70 billion. Reports indicate that these firms expect to receive only about 1% of their total order, or tens of thousands of units, over the next four months. NVIDIA has attributed the limited supply to ongoing production constraints and scheduling conflicts. While some shipments are expected by the end of the year, the company has indicated that supply will remain constrained for the foreseeable future.

news.summary: Major Chinese technology firms, including Alibaba, Tencent, and ByteDance, are reportedly receiving only a small fraction of their $70 billion order for NVIDIA RTX Pro 5500 chips due to production limitations.

news.content: Meta Platforms is entering the European debt market for the first time, offering euro-denominated bonds in six tranches with maturities ranging from approximately four years to over 38 years. This move follows the company's recent $15 billion U.S. dollar bond sale and is part of a broader strategy to fund significant investments in artificial intelligence. The shortest tranche was initially marketed at approximately 140 basis points over mid-swaps, while the longest was marketed at about 370 basis points over. This issuance marks the company's first debt offering outside of the United States.
news.headline: Meta Platforms Launches Debut Euro-Denominated Bond Sale
news.summary: Meta Platforms, Inc. has initiated its first-ever sale of euro-denominated debt, seeking to raise capital from European investors following a recent $15 billion U.S. dollar bond offering.

news.content: Meta has launched its Small Business Growth Academy in Sri Lanka in collaboration with local partner Roar AdX. The program is designed to help small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) enhance their digital presence and growth by providing training on advertising, Reels, and WhatsApp for Business. This initiative is part of Meta's broader expansion of the academy across 12 Asia-Pacific markets, aiming to build digital capability among entrepreneurs. The partnership combines Meta's platform expertise with Roar AdX's local market knowledge to support businesses in reaching customers and managing digital advertising more effectively.
news.headline: Meta Launches Small Business Growth Academy in Sri Lanka
news.summary: Meta has partnered with Roar AdX to introduce its Small Business Growth Academy in Sri Lanka, aiming to provide local entrepreneurs with digital marketing training and AI-enabled tools.

news.author: Anusuya Lahiri
news.content:
NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) stock gained more than 1% in Wednesday premarket trading as investors focused on resilient AI infrastructure demand, strong ecosystem commentary and continued constraints on advanced chip supply.

S&P 500 futures rose about 1%.

AMD And Super Micro Reinforce AI Demand

Recent results from key AI infrastructure players helped support sentiment around NVIDIA.

Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) CEO Lisa Su told analysts that revenue could grow more than 80% in 2027, while Super Micro Computer Inc. (NASDAQ:SMCI) reported fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenue of $19.9 billion and raised its full-year revenue outlook to $72 billion-$82 billion.

Those updates reinforced expectations that spending on AI compute and data-center infrastructure remains elevated.

Nvidia Prioritizes Higher-Margin AI Chips

Separately, NVIDIA is prioritizing production of its most advanced, higher-margin AI chips for customers such as OpenAI and Anthropic as global manufacturing capacity remains tight.

That strategy is limiting how quickly the company can satisfy strong Chinese demand for the export-permitted RTX Pro 5500, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday.

Chinese cloud and AI companies including Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. (NYSE:BABA), Tencent Holdings Ltd. (OTC:TCEHY) and ByteDance have reportedly ordered about 6 million RTX Pro 5500 chips, worth roughly $70 billion, but expect to receive only a small fraction over the next several months.

TSMC Capacity Remains A Constraint

NVIDIA relies on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. (NYSE:TSM) for production and is allocating more manufacturing capacity toward next-generation products such as Rubin.

That shift is expected to keep RTX Pro 5500 supply constrained.

Chinese buyers estimate deliveries could reach roughly 700,000 units by the end of 2027 as NVIDIA expands production, although actual shipment levels will depend on available capacity.

Technical Analysis

NVIDIA trades at $209.47, leaving the stock below its major short- and medium-term moving averages.

It sits about 3.7% below its 20-day SMA of $217.99, 5.2% below its 50-day SMA of $221.46 and 2.2% below its 100-day SMA of $214.55.

However, the stock remains roughly 2.6% above its 200-day SMA of $204.56, keeping the longer-term trend intact even as the near-term rebound remains unconfirmed.

Earnings And Analyst Outlook

NVIDIA is scheduled to report earnings on Nov. 17, 2026.

Consensus calls for EPS of $2.48, up from $1.30 a year earlier, and revenue of $109.17 billion, compared with $57.01 billion last year.

The stock trades at a 26.1-times P/E multiple.

NVIDIA carries a Buy consensus rating with an average price forecast of $341.04.

Recent analyst actions include Melius Research maintaining Buy while lowering its forecast to $315, Needham maintaining Buy with a $300 forecast, and Cantor Fitzgerald maintaining Overweight with a $350 forecast.

NVDA Stock Price Activity: NVIDIA shares were up 1.32% at $209.42 during premarket trading on Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

Image via Shutterstock

news.headline: What Is Going On With Nvidia Stock on Wednesday?
news.summary: NVIDIA stock gains over 1% to $209 premarket as resilient AI infrastructure demand and tight TSMC manufacturing capacity outweigh near-term export constraints.

news.author: Lekha Gupta
news.content:
Navitas Semiconductor Corp. (NASDAQ:NVTS) stock rose in Wednesday’s premarket trading after the company reported better-than-expected third-quarter results and issued an upbeat fourth-quarter revenue forecast.

The chipmaker also outlined plans to expand its artificial intelligence infrastructure business as it shifts away from mobile and consumer markets.

Navitas Beats Earnings Estimates, Raises AI Ambitions

Navitas reported an adjusted loss of 3 cents per share, narrower than analysts’ expected loss of 4 cents.

Revenue reached $13.99 million, beating the $13.17 million consensus estimate.

For the fourth quarter, Navitas forecasts revenue of $15.5 million to $16.5 million, above Wall Street’s $15.12 million estimate. The company expects a gross margin of 40.5%, plus or minus 100 basis points.

Navitas expects full-year 2026 revenue to grow about 7%, as demand from high-power markets offsets weaker mobile sales.

On Tuesday’s earnings call, CEO Chris Allexandre said Navitas expects its AI infrastructure business to triple in 2027, driven by accelerating demand for high-power solutions.

The company expects AI infrastructure to account for more than 40% of total revenue by the end of 2026. Allexandre also highlighted a strong order backlog extending into mid-2027.

Margins Improve As Cash Reserves Remain Strong

Adjusted gross margin rose 50 basis points sequentially to 40%, marking its third straight quarterly improvement.

Navitas ended the quarter with $531.5 million in cash. After a $126 million payment for its Claros acquisition, its pro forma cash balance stood at approximately $405 million.

The company reported no debt and said it has enough liquidity to support its growth plans.

See More: Top Value Stocks

NVIDIA Partnership and 800V Technology Fuel Expansion

Navitas identified four AI infrastructure opportunities: pre-800V power systems, 800V sidecar racks, native 800V architectures and grid modernization.

Native 800V products could enter production by late 2027, with broader growth expected in 2028.

The Claros acquisition adds voltage regulator technology for AI processors, strengthening Navitas’ silicon carbide and gallium nitride portfolio.

Navitas also announced 800V collaborations with NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Microchip Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MCHP), licensed GeneSiC technology to MagnaChip and secured a U.S. government selection to develop 10 kV silicon carbide chips.

Its GlobalFoundries partnership delivered the first U.S.-manufactured fifth-generation GaNFast wafers.

The company also introduced an Integrated Fabless Manufacturing strategy to expand production capacity through technology ownership and manufacturing partnerships.

NVTS Price Action: Navitas Semiconductor shares were up 9.93% at $9.41 during premarket trading on Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

Photo via Shutterstock

news.summary: Navitas (NVTS) stock jumped nearly 10% on a Q3 earnings beat, upbeat Q4 guidance, and expanding AI infrastructure deals.

news.author: Tanya Rawat
news.content:
Pharmaceutical executives say human biology is too complicated for artificial intelligence (AI) to cure disease on its own, with AstraZeneca PLC (NYSE: AZN) CEO Pascal Soriot saying, "Disease is complicated, biology is complicated."

No drug designed by AI has won Food and Drug Administration clearance, and drugmaker executives say AI helps researchers pick targets and identify suitable patients but cannot resolve biology’s unknowns alone, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday.

Soriot noted that, “to say AI is going to cure cancer is maybe a little bit of a jump,” the report added.

Silicon Valley’s Big AI Cure Claims

Anthropic (NASDAQ: ANT) CEO Dario Amodei posted on X in September that curing most human disease in five to 10 years may be possible. Anthropic has bought a stealth-mode biotech and a one-person biotech, and OpenAI bought an AI drug-discovery biotech in October.

Drugmakers Push Back

Jeff Leiden, executive chairman of Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated (NASDAQ: VRTX) recalled a tech leader claiming AI would cure 90% of human disease in seven years. "That’s complete BS," he said. Vertex used roughly 50 AI companies to comb through its data set of 10,000 drug compounds, and none generated a working drug, he said, according to the report.

Leiden was not the only research leader to question how far AI can go on its own. George Yancopoulos, president and chief scientific officer of Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Inc (NASDAQ: REGN) said AI will assist in the lab but will not "just miraculously come in and tell us how to do things," the report added.

Consultants who track the field point to a specific scientific hurdle. McKinsey & Company senior partner Alex Devereson, who focuses on AI in drug development, said around a quarter of mid-stage to late-stage drug failures trace to "off-target" safety problems, meaning unintended effects in the body, which current AI models struggle to predict, the report noted.

Read Also: Ro Khanna Calls For ‘Next New Deal’ After Democratic Midterm Wins, Lays Out $25 Living Wage, Medicare for All and Billionaire Taxes: ‘Make Trump Hoover If He Vetoes It’

Where AI Fits Into Pharma’s Future

AstraZeneca has already announced a collaboration with Insitro, an AI-driven drug developer, to discover treatments for complex liver and heart diseases, paying $40 million upfront. Insitro could also receive about $1.46 billion in milestone payments, for a potential total near $1.5 billion.

Generate Biomedicines co-founder and CTO Gevorg Grigoryan had said in an email interview that Nvidia Corp‘s (NASDAQ: NVDA) GPUs are "essential" for designing AI-generated medicines, but that "compute alone is not a differentiator." He said the companies most likely to lead AI drug discovery will combine computing with "proprietary biological data, experimental measurement scale, and the ability to close the loop between generation and measurement."

news.summary: Drugmaker executives doubt AI will cure disease soon, saying biology is too complicated.

news.author: Anusuya Lahiri
news.content:
Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. (NYSE:BABA) stock rose nearly 4% in Wednesday’s premarket trading as improving sentiment toward Chinese equities coincided with the company’s push to expand its Qwen artificial intelligence ecosystem.

China Policy Support Boosts Sentiment

The gains followed reports that the People’s Bank of China plans to meet with regulators and major banks to discuss improvements to a lending program that supports share buybacks and increased shareholdings.

The discussions follow a difficult October for Chinese equities. The CSI 300 fell 8.5% and recorded 12 consecutive weekly declines.

The policy developments helped lift Chinese stocks, suggesting Alibaba’s gains were part of a broader market rebound.

Apple Partnership Expands Qwen’s Reach

Separately, Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) plans to integrate Alibaba’s Qwen AI models into Apple Intelligence in China, with a rollout expected in December.

Qwen will support Siri, writing tools and visual intelligence. These features include text generation, image creation and document analysis, Asia News Network reported Monday.

CEO Eddie Wu said the partnership would bring new AI-powered experiences to Chinese consumers.

Alibaba Turns AI Into Consumer Products

Alibaba is also expanding Qwen’s commercial reach through its e-commerce platforms.

During Singles’ Day, a Taobao and Tmall livestream sold nearly 100,000 QwenWork monthly subscriptions in about 30 minutes.

The sales represented roughly 2 trillion AI tokens, the South China Morning Post reported Tuesday, citing company data.

Alibaba has also introduced AI tokens as a separate product category on Tmall. Its AI hardware offerings include laptops, voice recorders and desktop robots.

See More: Top Quality Stocks

Open-Source AI Drives Expansion

Chairman Joe Tsai said open-source technology remains central to Alibaba’s AI strategy.

Qwen now has more than 470 open-source variants, over 4 billion downloads and more than 330,000 derivative models, according to a South China Morning Post report Tuesday.

Tsai said Alibaba is using roughly $25 billion in free cash flow from its core e-commerce business to fund AI development.

The company has also doubled its computing capital spending annually over the past three years.

AI Chip Shortages Pose Challenges

Alibaba and other Chinese technology giants continue to face limited access to advanced AI processors.

Chinese companies reportedly ordered about 6 million NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) RTX Pro 5500 chips. However, they expect only a small portion of those orders to arrive over the coming months.

The shortages could increase demand for Alibaba’s in-house T-Head chips and domestic AI infrastructure.

Earnings And Analyst Outlook

Alibaba is expected to report earnings Nov. 24, 2026.

Analysts forecast earnings of $1.39 per share, up from 61 cents a year earlier. Revenue is expected to reach $40.35 billion, compared with $34.81 billion last year.

The stock trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of 22.5.

ETF Exposure

Alibaba has a 2.49% weighting in the Schwab Emerging Markets Equity ETF (NYSE:SCHE), a 1.50% weighting in the JPMorgan ActiveBuilders Emerging Markets Equity ETF (NASDAQ:JEMA) and a 1.84% weighting in the Russell Investments Emerging Markets Equity ETF (NASDAQ:REMG).

Fund inflows and outflows could influence demand for Alibaba shares.

news.content:
Third-quarter financial data indicates that international semiconductor foundries and memory manufacturers surpassed all publicly traded U.S. corporations, including Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA), in free cash flow generation.

The Free Cash Flow Leaders

During episode 212 of the “Facts Versus Feelings” podcast, Chief Macro Strategist Sonu Varghese detailed the current distribution of capital within the artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor industries.

Varghese stated, “Three memory makers, right? Samsung, SK Hynix Inc. (NASDAQ:SKHY), and Micron, plus TSMC [Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited (NYSE: TSM)], each generated more free cash flow in the third quarter than any other listed U.S. company, including Nvidia.”

This capital accumulation highlights the supply chain mechanics underlying current hardware investments. Varghese explained that when technology companies purchase processing units, “those actually include memory chips made by Micron and then you have also have Samsung and SK Hynix in the mix as well,” before Nvidia applies its own margin.

Read Also: CRWV, APLD, IREN Stocks Slip as Brad Gerstner Warns Democratic Midterm Gains Could Put 10–15 GW of AI Data Center Capacity at Risk

Capital Expenditure Shifts

The high free cash flow among memory manufacturers is driven by unprecedented capital expenditure from technology companies building out data centers.

Varghese noted that hyperscaler free cash flow is currently negative $40 billion and is “expected to stay negative through 2027.” Describing this dynamic, Varghese observed, “what’s happening is the buyer’s cash flow is going straight to the sellers.”

Overall spending by these buyers continues to scale up rapidly. Varghese stated that capital expenditure estimates for the major hyperscalers in 2027 have increased to $1.15 trillion, a figure he noted is up 94% from initial estimates.

When factoring in additional firms, Varghese noted that six hyperscalers are “expected to spend $1.4 trillion” in 2027, representing “almost 4% of GDP.”

Reinvestment by Memory Makers

While these memory manufacturers are currently generating high free cash flow, they are simultaneously directing funds back into infrastructure.

Varghese noted that “the capex for these memory makers… that’s doubled over the past year.” Looking forward, Varghese projects that aggregate free cash flow for chipmakers overall, specifically naming Nvidia, Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU), Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO), and Applied Materials Inc. (NASDAQ:APLD), is “expected to climb to 150, 200 billion by the end of 2027.”

U.S. stocks rose on Wednesday, as the Dow Jones, S&P 500, and Nasdaq 100 index futures advanced, following Tuesday’s mixed close.

According to the ADP employment report,  U.S. private sector employment saw a moderate boost, with companies adding 86,000 jobs in October as job-changers were enticed by higher pay, bonuses, and more hours.
However, the broader economic picture reflects a slight narrowing in the U.S. goods and services trade deficit, which declined by $0.7 billion to $105.0 billion in September, driven primarily by an increase in exports.

Democrats won control of both the Senate and the House in the midterm elections, according to The Associated Press. Iran’s Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf criticized President Donald Trump’s military campaign, while Trump told The Wall Street Journal that the Iran conflict contributed to Republican losses but said, "I did the right thing. I would have done it again."

The Associated Press also reported Democrats won 219 House seats to Republicans’ 126 and won 53 Senate seats to Republicans’ 41, with final results still pending.

Meanwhile, the 10-year Treasury bond yielded 4.93%, and the 2-year Treasury bond yielded 4.61% at the last check. The CME Group’s FedWatch tool projections show markets pricing in a 79.2% likelihood of the Federal Reserve hiking interest rates after its December meeting.

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY), the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (NASDAQ:QQQ) and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (NYSE:DIA), which track the S&P 500 index, Nasdaq 100 index and Dow Jones Industrial Average, respectively, were higher in premarket trading on Wednesday. Cues From Last Session

U.S. stocks closed mixed on Tuesday, with information technology, communication services, and industrials leading and consumer staples, materials, and energy lagging. The Dow dropped over 100 points.

Insights From Analysts

Ryan Detrick’s historical data showed that a divided congressional government produces the highest average returns for the S&P 500. At the same time, a Republican president paired with a Democratic Congress has delivered the lowest historical market gains.

Detrick said, “The worst possible combination is a Republican President and a Democratic Congress,” and he pegged that setup’s average annual S&P 500 return at 4.9%.

He added, “Futures seem to agree so far.” Addressing whether the 4.9% was driven by the Global Financial Crisis, Detrick said, “It is the most likely scenario at 22 times. So it is somewhat, but some other bad years in there for sure.”

Detrick also wrote, “Good reminder that the best scenario for stocks is a split Congress,” and said, “A Democrat controlled Congress is the worst scenario historically,” citing a 15.1% average annual return for a split Congress and a 6.7% average for a Democrat-controlled Congress.

Dan Ives, technology analyst and Yorkville Ives & Co. partner and senior managing director, said Democratic control of Congress could slow the U.S. artificial-intelligence (AI) infrastructure buildout, estimating that 10% of planned data centers "will not happen now."

Ives Sees Slower Data Center Expansion

Ives said Wednesday that the "Democratic blue tidal wave across the Senate and House" represented a "seismic shift" for the AI infrastructure story.

He said the election result "will have a negative impact on the pace of the AI Revolution buildout in the US over the next few years" and could slow the pace of the planned 800 to 1,000 data centers across the country.

"We estimate 10% of datacenters will not happen now," Ives wrote on X, adding that some investors may favor a slower construction pace while others could view it as additional risk.

Democrats secured control of both the House and Senate in Tuesday’s midterm elections, according to the Associated Press. The party also scored gubernatorial victories, including Gina Hinojosa’s defeat of Republican Gov. Greg Abbott in Texas.

Read Also: 'Worst Possible Combination:' Top Analyst Warns of Trump White House With Democratic Congress — Here's What the S&P 500 Has Historically Averaged

Thorne Rejects End Of AI Trade, Schiff Points To Economy

James E. Thorne, chief market strategist at Wellington-Altus, pushed back against expectations that slower construction would end the AI investment cycle.

"Expect the doomer narrative to shift: America won’t build the data centers, and the AI trade is over. Wrong on both counts," Thorne wrote on X.

He added that slowing data-center construction and ending the Iran war would be positive for bringing inflation down.

Economist Peter Schiff, meanwhile, characterized the Democratic victory as a judgment on President Donald Trump’s economic record.

Schiff called the election a "referendum on Trump," saying voters experienced economic hardship while Trump had been "boasting of a booming economy."

Gerstner Also Flags Capacity Risk

The comments followed a warning from Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner, who said on the All-In Podcast election-night livestream that 10 to 15 gigawatts of expected data-center capacity could fail to come online.

"I think it’s going to be really challenging for the AI infra," Gerstner said.

Still, Gerstner said he did not expect America to retreat from AI, calling it a global race.

How Has the Stock Market Performed?

The S&P 500 index has advanced 10.36% year-to-date. Similarly, the Nasdaq Composite index was up 9.19%, and the Dow Jones gained 7.04% YTD.

On Tuesday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY) and Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (NASDAQ:QQQ), which track the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100, respectively, closed mixed. SPY rose 0.30% to $754.35, while QQQ advanced 0.62% to $685.28. Meanwhile, the Dow tracker, State Street SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (NYSE:DIA), ended 0.44% lower at $517.06.

In premarket trading on Wednesday, SPY was up 1.12%, QQQ advanced 0.35%, and DIA rose 2.10%.

CoreWeave Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWV) and its peers are trading lower Wednesday after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections, with the flip of the Texas governor’s mansion drawing the most concern from investors.

  • CoreWeave stock is taking a hit today. What’s weighing on CRWV shares?

Democrat Gina Hinojosa Wins in Texas After Campaigning for a Data Center Moratorium

According to CNBC, AI data center stocks came under pressure after Democrats, seen as proponents of moratoriums on data center buildouts, won big in the midterms and in key technology hubs like Texas. State Rep. Gina Hinojosa won the Texas governor’s race over incumbent Republican Gov. Greg Abbott after campaigning for tougher limits on data center development, including an immediate moratorium in the state. Texas accounts for 27% of planned data center gigawatts, according to Wells Fargo. Democrats also won or retained the governorships in other major data center states, Georgia, Pennsylvania and Ohio, which represent 7%, 5% and 5% of planned U.S. data center gigawatts, according to Wells Fargo estimates.

"The midterm elections will slow the pace of data center buildouts across the U.S.," Dan Ives, partner at Yorkville Ives & Co., said in a note Wednesday. He called the Texas race the "biggest worry" of the night for investors in the AI trade.

CoreWeave Falls 7% While Peers and SpaceX Also Decline

CoreWeave fell 7% and IREN Limited (NASDAQ:IREN) fell 6%, CNBC reported. Nebius Group N.V. (NASDAQ:NBIS) was down 3% and Oracle Corporation (NYSE:ORCL) shed 4.3%, and Nvidia Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) was slightly lower. SpaceX Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX), which is building multiple gigawatts of data center capacity including projects in Texas, fell 7%. Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL), Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) and Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) mostly bucked the trend and were higher.

The Texas result adds to pressure on the AI trade, after the Nasdaq-100 fell into correction territory at the end of October on concerns that data center spending growth was slowing. Wells Fargo chief equity strategist Ohsung Kwon had warned in a report this week that a Democratic win in Texas could be a "left-tail event" for the AI trade.

news.content:
Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives doesn’t want to downplay the impact the Democratic Party’s win in the 2026 midterms could have on the artificial intelligence sector and buildout of data centers. Here’s what Ives said the morning after the election.

Dan Ives on "Blue Tidal Wave"

Ives says the Democratic Party’s wins in the House of Representatives and the Senate are a "big hurdle for AI buildout," which will impact the AI trade.

"The Democratic blue tidal wave across the Senate and House was a seismic shift that will have a negative impact on the pace of the AI Revolution buildout in the US over the next few years," Ives said in a new investor note.

Ives said the election result will "slow the pace" of data centers being built out, which will slow down the AI Revolution.

"There is no way to sugarcoat that Democrats taking control especially over the Senate will create some major hurdles for AI and tech legislation in the Beltway over the next two years."

With President Donald Trump threatening to veto potential laws brought forth by the Democratic Party, Ives says big tech CEOs will be forced to come to the "negotiating table" and come up with compromises with Congress for AI-related legislation.

Ives said that Texas could be among the biggest worries for tech investors with Democrat Gina Hinojosa winning the governor’s race in an upset over incumbent Greg Abbott. The analyst says Hinojosa is a "known anti-data center politician."

"Worries around the future of the data center buildout in Texas a real issue for tech investors."

The analyst highlights Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX), or SpaceX, as a stock that will be under pressure from the election result.

Ives said the election results and a slowdown in U.S. AI growth could help China narrow America’s lead, or even move ahead.

Read Also: Elon Musk vs. Tesla? His Midterm Money Could Work Against His Own Cars

Ives Still Bullish on Tech

While AI growth may slow, Ives is not ready to throw in the towel on the sector yet.

"It does not change the overall thesis and monetization theme of the AI Revolution," Ives said.

Even if fewer data centers get built, Ives said the Street is "way underestimating" future revenue growth from AI.

"Now it will happen at a more measured pace which is likely a good thing in the eyes of many investors…and the market will digest this news and move forward."

Ives said his "tech winner list" is unchanged.

The analyst recently shared what he believes are the best AI stocks across several sub-sectors.

  • Chips: Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA)
  • Hyperscalers: Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT)
  • Software: Palantir Technologies Inc. (NASDAQ:PLTR)
  • Cybersecurity: CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWD)
  • Consumer Internet: Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
  • Physical AI: Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA)

“Each sits where demand is contracted, funded, and accelerating, and together they give investors exposure to the AI buildout into 2027 without having to pick the winner of the application-layer shakeout,” Ives recently said.

Coherent Corp. (NYSE:COHR) reports fiscal first-quarter earnings after the bell Wednesday, with its conference call at 4:30 p.m. ET.

Wall Street expects adjusted earnings of about $2 per share on revenue near $2.31 billion.

Coherent’s data center revenue surged 66% year over year last quarter, yet shares have plunged nearly 42% since that report, raising doubts that manufacturing can keep up with demand.

On Kalshi, traders are betting on which words CEO Jim Anderson and his team will say.

What Kalshi Predicts Coherent Will Say

“Indium Phosphide” leads at 97%. Coherent uses the material to make lasers for AI data centers, but its factories cannot make laser chips fast enough to meet demand. Its fix is switching from three-inch to six-inch wafers, which yield four times as many chips at half the cost.

“Nvidia” trades at 80%. Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) invested $2 billion in Coherent in March and committed to purchasing billions of dollars of its products. Revenue from lasers covered by the partnership is expected to begin ramping in the December quarter.

"Multi-Rail" sits at 67%. The technology lets AI companies transmit more data between distant data centers using less equipment and power. Coherent sees a market above $2 billion by 2030, with initial revenue expected in the first half of 2027.

"Zurich" trades at 64%. Coherent plans to begin six-inch indium phosphide production at its Swiss factory in the first half of 2027, joining its existing six-inch lines in Texas and Sweden.

“Thermal Management” stands at 63%, while “Thermadite” trades at 58%. The company’s diamond-based cooling material conducts heat roughly twice as effectively as copper. Customers are testing samples, although revenue is not expected to ramp until the second half of 2027.

“Silicon Photonics” sits at 52%. Coherent launched its PhotonLink platform in September, combining lasers and optical components for next-generation AI networking. Initial revenue is expected in the December quarter.

What Kalshi Predicts Coherent Will Skip

"Optical Circuit Switch" trades at just 30%, with "Liquid Crystal" at 23%. Coherent’s optical switches use liquid-crystal technology, and the company has estimated the market could reach $4 billion by 2030. Executives often say "OCS" or "Optical Circuit Switching," neither of which counts under Kalshi’s rules.

“Apple” sits at 26%, despite Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) signing an expanded multiyear agreement last year for Coherent lasers used in iPhone and iPad Face ID systems.

"American Manufacturing" trades at 16% and "CHIPS Act" at 13%. Coherent signed a letter of intent in June for up to $50 million in federal funding to expand its Texas plant, but traders expect little talk of subsidies.

Reading the Board

Coherent isn’t short of customers. Anderson said in August that fiscal 2027 production capacity was essentially sold out, with orders extending into 2028.

The challenge is meeting that demand profitably. Coherent aims to grow quarterly revenue from $2.05 billion to more than $3 billion by June 2027, but capital spending reached $556 million last quarter.

Adjusted gross margin stood at 40.2%, below the company’s longer-term target of more than 42%.

Wall Street expects $2.54 billion in December-quarter revenue. Guidance will show whether the expansion is paying off.

Options imply an 11.7% move, putting roughly $4.8 billion in market value on the line.

news.content:
Intel Corp. (NASDAQ:INTC) has given back more than half of its 2026 rally in four months.

The stock touched an intraday record of $142.35 on June 30, putting the chipmaker’s market value near $756 billion. Shares closed Tuesday near $60.55, according to Benzinga Pro data, leaving Intel worth about $322 billion.

Roughly $434 billion has disappeared. Both values are estimates based on Intel’s current count of about 5.31 billion shares.

Q3 Beat Overshadowed by Q4 Guidance

The selling picked up speed after Intel’s third-quarter report last week.

Intel said revenue climbed 21% from a year earlier to $16.5 billion, and non-GAAP earnings reached 52 cents per share. Data center and AI revenue jumped 78% to $7.3 billion. CFO David Zinsner called it the strongest data center growth in 15 years.

Guidance for the current quarter disappointed. Intel forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, with non-GAAP EPS of 25 cents. The outlook came in weaker than expected as global PC sales slowed. Zinsner also said he expects the PC slowdown to last at least through the first half of next year.

Intel shares dropped about 29% the day after the print, their worst day since the 1970s.

Read Also: Nvidia, AMD, Marvell Targets Cut: Melius Pulls Back on AI Stocks as Big Tech Lines Up to Raise Cash

The chart below shows the 1-year performance of INTC:

Downgrades Pile Up

Analysts headed for the sidelines. Bank of America, Roth Capital and Seaport Research each downgraded Intel to Neutral from Buy.

Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya said the company "has not communicated enough traction with external foundry customers," according to CNBC.

Price targets came down across the Street. UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri cut his target to $80 from $100, while Barclays analyst Tom O’Malley lowered his to $75 from $100.

Uncle Sam’s INTC Stake

Taxpayers are feeling it too. The U.S. government became Intel’s largest shareholder after taking a 10% stake in August 2025, and the Oct. 30 plunge alone cut more than $11 billion from the stake’s value.

Measured from Intel’s peak, the losses run deeper. The government’s 433 million shares were worth about $61.6 billion at the June 30 high. At Tuesday’s close, their value stood near $26.2 billion, with roughly $35 billion in paper value erased.

See More: Top Quality Stocks

What Comes Next for Intel

Intel still has a financial cushion. Investments from the government and Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) have shored up its balance sheet. The company held $21.84 billion in cash and cash equivalents at the end of September, against $46.32 billion in long-term debt.

Bank of America’s comments on foundry customers point to the bigger question hanging over the stock. Data center sales are surging, but the foundry business still needs outside customers to justify the comeback story Wall Street bought into this summer.
